subject: Architecture
title: The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge: Earthquake Survivor
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge: Earthquake Survivor.

hook.text: The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge spans 6,532 feet — nearly a mile and a quarter — the longest suspension span.

buildup.text: Two towers rise 928 feet above sea level, supporting cables containing 300,000 miles of steel wire.

discovery.text: During construction, the 1995 Kobe earthquake shifted the two towers three feet farther apart.

twist.text: Engineers had built in enough tolerance. They simply adjusted the deck design to fit the new span length.

climax.text: Tuned mass dampers and pendulums in each tower counteract typhoon winds and earthquake forces.

punchline.text: An earthquake moved the bridge. The bridge didn't care.

quiz.question: What happened to the Akashi Kaikyo Bridge during the 1995 Kobe earthquake?
options: One tower partially collapsed and was rebuilt
The towers shifted three feet apart, and the design was adjusted
The main cables snapped and had to be replaced
